name: How do you decide between remodeling and rebuilding an apartment property?

mainEntity.name: When is it smarter to renovate an existing apartment building instead of starting over with new construction?
mainEntity.text: When is it smarter to renovate an existing apartment building instead of starting over with new construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: The choice between remodeling and rebuilding depends on the building’s condition, layout, and long-term economics. Remodeling can be the better option if the structure is sound, the site is favorable, and the upgrades can substantially improve rents without major structural changes. Rebuilding may be smarter when the property is obsolete, inefficient, or limited by code, parking, or structural problems that are too expensive to solve through renovation. In Los Angeles, the decision often comes down to whether the existing building can compete with newer product after renovation. If the layout is poor or the systems are outdated, a remodel may not create enough value. Owners should compare the cost of deep renovation against the cost of replacement, including permitting, financing, and downtime. The right choice is the one that gives the best long-term return with the least execution risk.
acceptedAnswer.description: Remodeling makes sense when the structure, layout, and site are still strong and the upgrade cost is well below replacement cost. Rebuilding is often better when the building is outdated, inefficient, or constrained by major structural, code, or site problems.
